title: Form 1065 and a partner's K-1 — Cedar Partners
instructions: Cedar Partners is a calendar-year general partnership. Anika is a **40%** general partner. Compute the partnership's ordinary business income, her K-1 amounts, and her year-end basis.

exhibits.title: 2025 partnership items
exhibits.content:
| Item | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Sales | 1,200,000 |
| Cost of goods sold | 500,000 |
| Employee salaries | 200,000 |
| Guaranteed payment to Anika | 80,000 |
| Rent | 60,000 |
| MACRS depreciation | 50,000 |
| Business meals (50% deductible) | 6,000 |
| §179 expense | 30,000 |
| Charitable contributions | 10,000 |
| Qualified dividends | 20,000 |
| Municipal bond interest | 4,000 |
| Long-term capital gain | 16,000 |
| §1231 gain | 12,000 |

exhibits.title: Anika
exhibits.content:
- Beginning outside basis: **$50,000**
- Her share of partnership liabilities increased by **$10,000**
- Cash distributions to Anika: **$40,000**

rows.label: Anika's share of ordinary business income
Anika's total ordinary income from Cedar
Anika's ending outside basis
rows.explanation: 50,000 + 10,000 liabilities + 122,800 + 8,000 dividends + 1,600 municipal + 6,400 LTCG + 4,800 §1231 − 40,000 distribution − 1,200 nondeductible meals − 12,000 §179 − 4,000 charity = **146,400**. The guaranteed payment doesn't affect basis.

rows.label: Guaranteed payment
rows.explanation: Deducted in OBI and reported separately to the recipient.

rows.label: Original due date of Cedar's 2025 Form 1065
rows.explanation: 15th day of the 3rd month; March 15, 2026 is a Sunday.
